# Book I, Proposition 47

*The theorem of Pythagoras*

> In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/47-idea.svg" alt="Count the little squares: 9 and 16 make 25. Euclid proves it for every right-angled triangle, and never counts anything." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>Count the little squares: 9 and 16 make 25. Euclid proves it for every right-angled triangle, and never counts anything.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/47.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.47, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;

I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.

For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB, HC; [I. 46] through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE, and let AD, FC be joined.

Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with AG. [I. 14]

For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.

And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]

And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]

Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]

And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]

[But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]

Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.

Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]

And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.

Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

```lean
/-- Where the squares fall. If the angle `ABC` is less than a right angle, and `BD`
stands at right angles to `BC` on the other side of it from `A`, then `C` lies within
the angle `ABD`: on `A`'s side of `BD`, and on `D`'s side of `BA`. Euclid reads this
off his figure when he adds the angle `ABC` to the right angles `DBC`, `FBA`, and
again when he takes the parallelograms `BL`, `CL` to make up the square `BDEC`.

The straight line `AD` crosses `BC`, since it joins points on either side of it. Not
at `B`, for then the angles `ABC`, `CBD` would make two right angles [I. 13], and
`CBD` alone is right. Not beyond `B` from `C`, for then the angle `ABD` would be
greater than two right angles: the angle on the far side of `AB` from `C` is
greater than right [I. 13], and to it is added the right angle on the far side of
`BD`. So it crosses on the ray from `B` through `C`, and `C` lies where the crossing
point does. [I. 13] -/
theorem Prop47.within {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C)
    (hCBD : ∠ C B D = ∟) (hacute : ∠ A B C < ∟) :
    SameSideOf C A B D ∧ SameSideOf C D B A := by
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  have hop : OppositeSides A D BC := hD.symm.oppositeSides hB_BC hC_BC
  have hA_BC : ¬ OnLine A BC := hop.1
  have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := hop.2.1
  /- `AD` crosses `BC` at a point `Y`. -/
  obtain ⟨Y, hY_BC, hAYD⟩ := OppositeSides.exists_between hop
  obtain ⟨AD, hA_AD, hD_AD⟩ := Postulate1 A D (ne_of_between_ends hAYD)
  have hY_AD : OnLine Y AD := on_line_of_between_ends hAYD hA_AD hD_AD
  have hBD : B ≠ D := fun e => hD_BC (e ▸ hB_BC)
  have hBA : B ≠ A := fun e => hA_BC (e ▸ hB_BC)
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
  obtain ⟨BA, hB_BA, hA_BA⟩ := Postulate1 B A hBA
  by_cases hYB : Y = B
  · /- Not at `B`: the angles `ABC`, `CBD` would make two right angles. [I. 13] -/
    exfalso
    rw [hYB] at hAYD hY_AD
    have hC : ¬ Collinear A D C := fun ⟨K, hA_K, hD_K, hC_K⟩ => by
      have hK : K = AD := line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hAYD) hA_K hD_K hA_AD hD_AD
      rw [hK] at hC_K
      exact hA_BC ((line_unique hABC.ne₂₃ hY_AD hC_K hB_BC hC_BC) ▸ hA_AD)
    have h13 := Prop13 hAYD hC
    rw [hCBD] at h13
    exact Magnitude.ne_of_lt (add_lt_add_right ∟ hacute) h13
  · have hB_AD : ¬ OnLine B AD := fun hB =>
      hA_BC ((line_unique hYB hY_AD hB hY_BC hB_BC) ▸ hA_AD)
    have hY_BD : ¬ OnLine Y BD := fun hY =>
      hD_BC ((line_unique hYB hY hB_BD hY_BC hB_BC) ▸ hD_BD)
    have hY_BA : ¬ OnLine Y BA := fun hY =>
      hA_BC ((line_unique hYB hY hB_BA hY_BC hB_BC) ▸ hA_BA)
    by_cases hYBC : Between Y B C
    · /- Not beyond `B`: the angle `ABD` would be greater than two right angles. -/
      exfalso
      have hADB : Triangle A D B := fun ⟨K, hA_K, hD_K, hB_K⟩ =>
        hB_AD ((line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hAYD) hA_K hD_K hA_AD hD_AD) ▸ hB_K)
      have hsum : ∠ A B D = ∠ A B Y + ∠ Y B D := angle_add_of_between hADB hAYD
      have hYCA : ¬ Collinear Y C A := fun ⟨K, hY_K, hC_K, hA_K⟩ =>
        hA_BC ((line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hYBC) hY_K hC_K hY_BC hC_BC) ▸ hA_K)
      have hYCD : ¬ Collinear Y C D := fun ⟨K, hY_K, hC_K, hD_K⟩ =>
        hD_BC ((line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hYBC) hY_K hC_K hY_BC hC_BC) ▸ hD_K)
      have h₁ : ∠ Y B A + ∠ A B C = ∟ + ∟ := Prop13 hYBC hYCA
      have h₂ : ∠ Y B D + ∠ D B C = ∟ + ∟ := Prop13 hYBC hYCD
      rw [(angle_symm hBD.symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm).trans hCBD] at h₂
      have hYBD : ∠ Y B D = ∟ := by
        rcases lt_trichotomy (∠ Y B D) ∟ with h | h | h
        · exact absurd h₂ (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (add_lt_add_right ∟ h))
        · exact h
        · exact absurd h₂.symm (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (add_lt_add_right ∟ h))
      have hgt : ∟ < ∠ A B Y := by
        have h₃ : ∠ A B C + ∠ Y B A < ∟ + ∠ Y B A := add_lt_add_right _ hacute
        rw [add_comm (∠ A B C), add_comm ∟, h₁] at h₃
        rw [angle_symm hBA.symm (ne_of_between hYBC)]
        exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_right h₃
      have h₄ : ∟ + ∟ < ∠ A B D := by
        rw [hsum, hYBD]
        exact add_lt_add_right ∟ hgt
      exact angle_le_two_right A B D h₄
    · /- So `Y` lies on the ray from `B` through `C`, and within the angle `ABD`. -/
      have hray : OnRay C B Y := OnRay.symm ⟨hABC.ne₂₃, hYB, ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, hY_BC⟩, hYBC⟩
      have h₁ : SameSideOf Y A B D :=
        SameSideOf.of_line hBD hB_BD hD_BD (pasch2 (between_symm hAYD) hD_BD hY_BD)
      have h₂ : SameSideOf Y D B A :=
        SameSideOf.of_line hBA hB_BA hA_BA (pasch2 hAYD hA_BA hY_BA)
      exact ⟨SameSideOf.of_onRay hray h₁, SameSideOf.of_onRay hray h₂⟩

/-- In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle. -/
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H := by
  -- Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;
  -- I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.
  -- For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB,
  -- HC; [I. 46]
  /- The three squares are given in the statement, so I.46 is not cited. Their
     opposite sides are parallel by `Prop28.square`. -/
  have hpsq : Parallelogram B D E C :=
    (Prop28.square hBDEC.rotate.rotate.rotate
      (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hD.symm hE.symm).swap).rotate
  have hABFGpar : Parallelogram A B F G :=
    Prop28.square hABFG (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hF.symm hG.symm)
  have hACKHpar : Parallelogram A C K H :=
    Prop28.square hACKH (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hK.symm hH.symm)
  obtain ⟨hBD_DE, hDE_EC, hEC_CB, hCBD, -, -, hECB⟩ := id hBDEC
  have hBD_BC : ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ :=
    hBD_DE.trans (hDE_EC.trans (hEC_CB.trans (len_symm C B)))
  have hCE_CB : ‖C E‖ = ‖C B‖ := (len_symm C E).trans hEC_CB
  have hBCE : ∠ B C E = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hE.triangle.ne₂₃.symm).trans hECB
  have hright' : ∠ C A B = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm).trans hright
  /- I.17 makes the angles at B and C acute. With the outward squares,
     `Prop47.within` puts A between the straight lines BD and CE. -/
  have hacB : ∠ A B C < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.2
    rw [hright'] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  have hacC : ∠ A C B < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.1
    rw [hright] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  obtain ⟨hCA_BD, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacB
  obtain ⟨hBA_CE, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.acb hE.swap hBCE hacC
  -- through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE,
  have hBD : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
  have hCE : C ≠ E := hBA_CE.1
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
  obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hCE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨DE, hD_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 D E hpsq.2.1
  have hBD_CE : Parallel BD CE := hpsq.1.parallel hB_BD hD_BD hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDE_BC : Parallel DE BC := hpsq.2.parallel hD_DE hE_DE hC_BC hB_BC
  have hA_BD : ¬ OnLine A BD :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD))
  obtain ⟨AL, hA_AL, hAL_BD⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BD
  have hA_CE : ¬ OnLine A CE :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE))
  have hAL_CE : Parallel AL CE :=
    Prop30.parallel hAL_BD hBD_CE.symm (fun e => hA_CE (e ▸ hA_AL))
  /- The parallel meets DE at L and BC at its unlettered foot. A straight
     line meeting one of two parallels meets the other:
     `Prop30.meet`, as Heath reports Proclus drawing it under I.31. -/
  have hDE_BD : DE ≠ BD := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hB_BD) hB_BC
  obtain ⟨L, hL_DE, hL_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hD_BD hD_DE hDE_BD
  have hBC_BD : BC ≠ BD := fun e => hD.triangle.off_line hB_BC hC_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨X, hX_BC, hX_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hB_BD hB_BC hBC_BD
  have hXL : X ≠ L := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_DE) hX_BC
  have hDL : D ≠ L := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AL) hD_BD
  have hXB : X ≠ B := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hX_AL) hB_BD
  have hLE : L ≠ E := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hL_AL (e ▸ hE_CE)
  have hCX : C ≠ X := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hX_AL (e ▸ hC_CE)
  have P₁ : Parallelogram B D L X :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hBD hXL.symm hB_BD hD_BD hL_AL hX_AL hAL_BD.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hDL hXB hD_DE hL_DE hX_BC hB_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have P₂ : Parallelogram X L E C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hXL hCE.symm hX_AL hL_AL hE_CE hC_CE hAL_CE,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hLE hCX hL_DE hE_DE hC_BC hX_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have hXLA : Collinear X L A := ⟨AL, hX_AL, hL_AL, hA_AL⟩
  -- and let AD, FC be joined.
  /- The joined straight lines are the sides of the triangles in I.4 below. -/
  -- Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA,
  -- and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make
  -- the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with
  -- AG. [I. 14]
  have hCAG : Between C A G := Prop14 hG.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright, angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm hG.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hABFG.2.2.2.1])
  -- For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.
  have hBAH : Between B A H := Prop14 hH.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright', angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hH.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hACKH.2.2.2.1])
  /- Euclid proves one half and then says "similarly". We give these sentences
     once over any letters, using the straightness and acute angle already
     proved, and apply them at B and at C. -/
  have half : ∀ {A B C D F G X L : Point}, Triangle A B C →
      ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ → ∠ C B D = ∟ → OppositeSidesOf D A B C →
      Square A B F G → OppositeSidesOf F C A B → Parallelogram A B F G →
      Between C A G → ∠ A B C < ∟ → Parallelogram X B D L → Collinear X L A →
      quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G := by
    intro A B C D F G X L hABC hBD hCBD hD hsq hF hpsq hCAG hacute hp hX
    obtain ⟨hAB_BF, -, -, -, hABF, -, -⟩ := hsq
    -- And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC
    -- be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]
    obtain ⟨hCA_BD, hCD_BA⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacute
    obtain ⟨hAC_BF, hAF_BC⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.cba hF.swap hABF
      (by rw [angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]; exact hacute)
    have hDBA : ∠ D B A = ∠ D B C + ∠ C B A :=
      angle_add_of_within hCA_BD hCD_BA
    have hFBC : ∠ F B C = ∠ F B A + ∠ A B C :=
      angle_add_of_within hAC_BF hAF_BC
    have hBD_ne : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
    have hBF_ne : B ≠ F := hAC_BF.1
    have hrights : ∠ D B C = ∠ F B A := by
      rw [angle_symm hBD_ne.symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm, hCBD,
        angle_symm hBF_ne.symm hABC.ne₁₂, hABF]
    have hadd := CommonNotion2 hrights (Eq.refl (∠ A B C))
    have hang : ∠ D B A = ∠ F B C := by
      rw [hDBA, hFBC, angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]
      exact hadd
    -- And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two
    -- sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base
    -- AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]
    have hABD : ∠ A B D = ∠ F B C :=
      (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂ hBD_ne.symm).trans hang
    obtain ⟨hAD_FC, h4, -, -⟩ :=
      Prop4 hCD_BA.symm.triangle hAC_BF.symm.triangle
        ((len_symm B A).trans hAB_BF) hBD hABD
    -- Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and
    -- are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]
    have h41a : quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := Prop41 hp hX
    -- And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and
    -- are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]
    obtain ⟨GC, hC_GC, hA_GC, hG_GC⟩ := collinear_of_between hCAG
    have h41b : quadArea G F B A = △ F C B + △ F C B :=
      Prop41 hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.reverse ⟨GC, hG_GC, hA_GC, hC_GC⟩
    -- [But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]
    have hdouble := CommonNotion2 h4 h4
    -- Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.
    calc
      quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := h41a
      _ = △ B F C + △ B F C := hdouble
      _ = △ F C B + △ F C B := by rw [area_bca B F C]
      _ = quadArea G F B A := h41b.symm
      _ = quadArea A B F G := by
        rw [quadArea_reverse, hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate]
  have h₁ : quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G :=
    half hABC hBD_BC hCBD hD hABFG hF hABFGpar hCAG hacB P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate hXLA
  -- Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the
  -- square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]
  have h₂ : quadArea X C E L = quadArea A C K H :=
    half hABC.acb hCE_CB hBCE hE.swap hACKH hK hACKHpar hBAH hacC P₂.reverse hXLA
  /- The foot of AL lies between B and C, and L between D and E: A lies
     between BD and CE, and AL is parallel to both (`Between.of_inside`). -/
  have ss : ∀ {P Q R : Point} {N : Line},
      SameSide P Q N → SameSide Q R N → SameSide P R N :=
    fun h₁ h₂ => same_side_trans (same_side_symm h₁) h₂
  have hAC_BD : SameSide A C BD := same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hAB_CE : SameSide A B CE := same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE)
  have hBXC : Between B X C :=
    Between.of_inside hB_BD hC_CE ⟨BC, hB_BC, hX_BC, hC_BC⟩
      (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD)
      (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE)
  have hCE_BD : SameSide C E BD :=
    same_side_symm (hpsq.sameSideOf.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hBD_CE' : SameSide B D CE := hpsq.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf.sameSide hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDLE : Between D L E :=
    Between.of_inside hD_BD hE_CE ⟨DE, hD_DE, hL_DE, hE_DE⟩
      (ss (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD) hCE_BD)
      (ss (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE) hBD_CE')
  have hwhole : quadArea B D E C = quadArea X B D L + quadArea X C E L := by
    rw [quadArea_add_of_parallelograms P₁ P₂ hBXC hDLE,
      P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse X C E L]
  have hequal := hwhole.trans (CommonNotion2 h₁ h₂)
  -- And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.
  /- These are the three given squares. -/
  -- Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.
```

<details><summary>The 61 things Euclid takes for granted here</summary>

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `D` is between `A` and `B`, then `D` is between `A` and `C`. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `C` is between `B` and `D`, then `B` is between `A` and `D`. (Between 5)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, it is between `C` and `A`. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L195): Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point `A` inside the second, and a point `B` outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between `B` and `C`. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L29): Let a point be taken on the straight line `L`. (Points 2)
- [`exists_point_on_line_off_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L34): Let a point be taken on `L`, not on the different straight line `M`. (Points 2, with "distinct from `M`")
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L46): Let a point be taken on the other side of `L` from `B`. (Points 6)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L38): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, heading out to a point `C` outside it, cuts the circle between `B` and `C`. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, produced beyond `B` away from `C`, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of `L` crosses `L`. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `A` is not between `B` and `C`. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and also between `A` and `D`, then `B` is not between `C` and `D`: `C` and `D` lie on the same side of `B`. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92): Points on one side of a line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56): A straight line through `A` and `B`, with `B` between `A` and `C`, passes through `C`. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61): A straight line through `A` and `C` passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, `A` is on `L` and `B` is off it, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `L`: a straight line that leaves `L` at `A` does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114): A line through a point between `A` and `C` separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119): If two different straight lines `L` and `M` meet at `B`, and `A` and `C` are points of `M`, different from each other and from `B`, that are not on the same side of `L`, then `B` is between `A` and `C`. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89): If `A` is on the same side of a straight line as `B`, then `B` is on the same side as `A`. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`. If `C` lies within the angle `BAD` (on `D`'s side of `L` and on `B`'s side of `N`), then `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`: the straight line `AC` separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`, with `B` other than `A` and `D` off `M`. If `C` and `D` are on the same side of `L`, and `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `N`: `C` lies within the angle `BAD`. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54): If `D` lies within the angle `BAC`, then `BAC` is made up of `BAD` and `DAC`. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_le_two_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L29): No angle exceeds two right angles. (Metric 5)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26): The angle `ABC` is the angle `CBA`. (Metric 4)
- [`area_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L88): Cutting a triangle in two from a vertex adds up. (Diagram-area 2)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_degenerate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L32): A "triangle" with a repeated corner has no area. (Metric 6)
- [`area_eq_zero_of_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L80): A "triangle" whose corners lie on one line has no area. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `CAB`. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `ACB`. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `AB` and `BC` together make up `AC`. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23): The line `AB` is the line `BA`. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49): If the angle `BAC` is nothing, `C` lies on the ray from `A` through `B`. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle `ABC` can be applied to the straight line `L` with `A` on `D`, `B` on the ray from `D` through `G`, and `C` on the side of `L` where `H` is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L22): Adding is associative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L25): Adding is commutative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L44): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L28): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L31): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L34): "Less than" is transitive. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L38): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L41): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

**Doubles of equal triangles.** Euclid proves the parallelogram BL equal to the square GB, as doubles of the equal triangles ABD, FBC (I.4, I.41), and says "similarly" for CL and HC. We write that half once, over any letters, and use it at B and at C. Heiberg brackets the sentence on doubles because it quotes a Common Notion itself interpolated, as Heath explains (vol. 1, p. 350); in Lean, Common Notion 2 adds the equal triangles to themselves.

**What the figure shows.** "Let the angle ABC be added to each" needs C within the angle DBA, and A within the angle FBC. Euclid reads both off his figure; Lean needs a reason. The angles at B and C are less than right angles (I.17), and the squares are described outward, so `Prop47.within` puts each point where the figure does, by I.13, and `angle_add_of_within` adds the angles. Our statement gives the three squares, so the bracketed I.46 is not cited, and `Prop28.square` brings in I.28 to make each one a parallelogram.

**Where AL falls.** "Through A let AL be drawn parallel" is I.31, though no bracket names it, and `Prop30.parallel` (I.30) makes AL parallel to CE as well. A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other, from I.30 (`Prop30.meet`). So AL meets DE at L, and BC at a point Heath leaves without a letter: it has a name in the Lean and none in the figure. Since A lies between BD and CE, `Between.of_inside` puts that point between B and C and L between D and E, and Book Zero's `quadArea_add_of_parallelograms` makes BL and CL the whole square.

**"I marvel more at the writer of the Elements."** Heath reports Proclus retelling the story that Pythagoras sacrificed an ox for this theorem, and adding: "But for my part, while I admire those who first observed the truth of this theorem, I marvel more at the writer of the Elements" (vol. 1, p. 350). Of the postulates, the certificate records 1 and 2 directly, the second for a straight line produced inside `Prop28.square`; the propositions I.47 cites bring in Postulates 1 to 4 as well, and Postulate 5 comes in through I.30 and I.41.

**The modern way.** Put A = (0, 0), B = (b, 0) and C = (0, c), and write a for BC. The foot of AL divides BC into b²/a and c²/a, so the rectangles BL and CL, of height a, have areas b² and c², and together they make the square on BC: b² + c² = a².

---

<sub>Euclid's text: T. L. Heath, The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements, vol. 1 (Cambridge, 1908), pp. 349–350; scan leaves n369–n370; figure on n369. Public domain.</sub>

<sub>The tacit rules follow the System E of Jeremy Avigad, Edward Dean and John Mumma, read alongside LeanEuclid (Logan Murphy, Kaiyu Yang, Jialiang Sun, Zhaoyu Li, Anima Anandkumar and Xujie Si).</sub>
